Let $u={log}_{4}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{log}_{4}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =2\int {log}_{4}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot {u}^{2}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot {log}_{4}^{2}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x{log}_{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{log}_{3}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{3}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot (\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{4}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{4{log}_{4}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =4{\int }_{1}^{4}{log}_{4}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{1}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡4{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot (1-0) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{3\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{1}^{e}\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{u}^{3/2}}{3/2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2({1}^{3/2}-{0}^{3/2}) \\  & =2(1-0) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
